# bytecode-budget real-trace fixtures (node v26.8.2)

Verbatim captures (S-9). Nothing in the `.txt` files was edited or truncated.

- Node: v26.8.2 (`node --version`)
- Host: Darwin arm64 (`uname -sm`)
- Date: 2026-11-02
- Driver: `driver.mjs` (ESM; `.mjs` chosen so the module type is unambiguous. A `.js` copy
  with no package.json also works: named functions get the same headers and lengths; only the
  anonymous functions differ. REPORTED, no capture kept (`--print-bytecode-filter=` on a
  `driver.js` copy in a dir with no package.json; node v26.8.2, Darwin arm64, 2026-11-02, 3/3 runs
  gave the same lengths; log: `.handoff/evidence/phase2/cjs.txt`): the CJS copy prints 6 anonymous functions
  (5, 119, 5, 354, 6, 6) against 5 for ESM (5, 119, 400, 6, 6): an extra 5-byte function, and the
  top-level function is 354 bytes as CJS vs 400 as ESM).

## Capture commands (run with cwd = this directory)

    env -u NODE_OPTIONS node --print-bytecode --print-bytecode-filter=<fn> driver.mjs > <file> 2>&1

`all.txt`: `env -u NODE_OPTIONS node --print-bytecode driver.mjs > all.txt 2>&1`
(identical size to `--print-bytecode-filter=*`). 54169 bytes, kept whole.

`limits.txt`: `node --v8-options | awk "$LIMITS_AWK"`
`v8-options-excerpt.txt`: `node --v8-options | grep -E 'inlined-bytecode-size|inline-budget'`

LIMITS_AWK and BYTECODE_AWK were taken from
`git show 7f0ba7b:inlining-budget-diff.sh` (a frozen copy sits in `.handoff/frozen/7f0ba7b/`) by `eval "$(sed -n "/^LIMITS_AWK='$/,/^'$/p" F)"`
(same for BYTECODE_AWK), not retyped. In that file they sit at lines 212-218 and 222-228.

Every run exited 0. All output goes to stdout; stderr was empty (no warnings).

## Facts

a. Block format: `[generated bytecode for function: NAME (0x<12-hex> <SharedFunctionInfo NAME>)]`,
   then `Bytecode length: N`, then `Parameter count P`, `Register count R`, `Frame size F`,
   then the bytecode listing, `Constant pool (size = n)` (+ entries), `Handler Table (size = n)`,
   `Source Position Table (size = n)`, and a `0x... <Other heap object (TRUSTED_BYTE_ARRAY_TYPE)>` line.
   `Bytecode length` is always the line right after the header. Anonymous functions print
   `function:  (0x... <SharedFunctionInfo>)]` (empty name, two spaces).

b. The filter matches the short function name EXACTLY: `rea` and `ead` print nothing. A trailing
   `*` is a prefix wildcard (`re*` printed the 4 `read`s), a leading `-` negates, `*` or an omitted
   filter prints everything. Names are NOT qualified: `Store.read` and `objA.read` print nothing;
   `read` prints 4 functions (top-level `read`, class method `Store.read`, object method
   `objA.read`, `objB.read: function (x)`). Getter header: `get value` (filter `value` prints
   nothing). Static method: `make`. Class constructor: `Store`. Repeated
   `--print-bytecode-filter` flags: the last one wins.

c. `lazy` (never called): empty output, exit 0 -> NO-VERDICT. With `--no-lazy` it prints
   (length 6).

d. Duplicates: `dup` prints 2 headers (6, 19); BYTECODE_AWK -> `6,19`. BYTECODE_AWK keeps
   DISTINCT VALUES in first-seen order: `read` (4 functions, 6,5,6,6) -> `6,5`. Two same-name
   functions with equal length collapse to one value.

e. Same stream, nothing else: no warnings, no internal builtins. With filter omitted, `*` or
   empty, 5 anonymous functions also print: two from node's internal main-module runner
   (5 bytes and 119 bytes; constant pool shows `internal/process/pre_execution`,
   `runMain`), the ESM top-level module function (400, empty name), and the two IIFE wrappers
   (6, 6). Top-level functions print only with filter empty, `*` or omitted (`-read` printed
   the 119 and the IIFEs but not the 5 or the 400).

f. 5 consecutive runs per filter (all 14 above): raw output differs run to run whenever
   anything printed (0x addresses; even the address width changes, 472 vs 475 bytes for add);
   after `sed -E 's/0x[0-9a-f]+/0x/g'` all 5 are byte-identical, including header order.

g. LIMITS_AWK output (limits.txt, 13 lines):
   max-maglev-inlined-bytecode-size=100, -cumulative=920, -small-total=3000, -small=27,
   -small-with-heapnum-in-out=75; max-inlined-bytecode-size=460, -cumulative=920,
   -absolute=4600, -small-total=30000, -small=30, -small-with-heapnum-in-out=75;
   reserve-inline-budget-scale-factor=1.2; max-maglev-eager-inlined-bytecode-size=30.
   The 75 HeapNumber limit is a real flag (TurboFan and Maglev both). Present in
   --v8-options but MISSED by LIMITS_AWK: `max-turbolev-eager-inlined-bytecode-size=30`.

h. No `--no-lazy` needed for a function called once (a scratch `once(3)` printed, length 6).
   Closures print when called (`inner`, 6). A closure inside a called function that is itself
   never called does not print.
